prompt:
Use the attached image as the reference: the same adult Scottish woman — the personification of Edinburgh — seen off duty in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye colour, hair colour, skin tone and body exactly; change only her clothes, pose and place. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

Output: one square 1:1 image, 1024×1024.

Face: exactly the attached image's face — the same short midface and face length-to-width ratio; the camera angle, pose, bangs or a headpiece never make her face look longer or her jaw heavier.

Style: Korean MMORPG character artwork. A painterly face with naturally observed facial anatomy, subtle eyelid structure, and soft, realistic shading across the nose and cheeks. 2D painting with visible brushwork: layered strokes of colour, soft broken edges, thin coloured linework and a few crisp accents on the face and costume.
SKIN FINISH: dewy, glass-like highlights on the skin of her shoulders, arms, collarbones and legs — a soft, luminous wet-look sheen that follows the body's forms; her face keeps a soft, natural finish.

She is strikingly beautiful and refined — harmonious features, clear luminous skin, graceful posture — while her own face stays distinct: her face shape, eyes, brows, nose and lips follow the attached image, not a generic pretty face.

World: an ordinary day in Edinburgh as her world knows it — a far-future city two centuries from now: sleek curved architecture, smart glowing materials, holographic interfaces, layered levels of the city and quiet flying vehicles; even an everyday place is rebuilt in that future, not today's Edinburgh with neon added. This is her world's own everyday life, not our present day: every made thing around her — tools, cups, lamps, signs, vehicles, money and devices — is made the way her world makes them.
Let the place itself carry this world through its materials, fittings and objects; do not add the city's landmarks, towers, giant holograms or a skyline unless the place below names them.

Place: the grassy path up the old volcano two centuries on, kept wild as it is, cliffs of columnar basalt beside her and the far-future city and its pale towers glittering below in early light.
Around her, as her world makes them: a smart bottle with a glowing level line; a holographic phone screen projected from her wrist; glowing wireless ear-pieces.
Season: summer — mild days rarely warmer than the low twenties, the whole city crowded and buzzing for its August festivals.
Weather: a windy day — a strong south-west wind whipping coats and hair and racing the clouds over the castle.
Time of day: dawn — the first pale light before the city wakes, the last lamps still lit and the streets quiet; a pale lilac sky, mist low on the ground.
Light direction: backlit — the main light comes from behind her, a bright rim along her hair and shoulders.
Outfit: a vintage aviatrix look — a cropped leather flight jacket over a fitted top, high-waisted jodhpurs, goggles pushed up on her head and tall boots — in a monochrome palette of black and charcoal with at most one white or grey accent; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance; fabric weight — its knit or thin-fabric pieces (a top, an inner top or a knit dress) are 40-denier yarn, semi-sheer so her skin tone and body line show softly through, with a fully opaque lining over the bust and the hips; any tights or stockings are sheer 25-denier nylon; shorts, skirts, leather and other heavy materials stay opaque; styled with a slim leather belt at the waist, worn with maximal styling presence — the chosen outfit worn in its most revealing version — a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders, a cropped or open-back cut, a short hem or high slit showing the thighs, as far as the outfit allows, skin clearly showing, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.
Her clothes are her world's everyday techwear — the chosen outfit keeps its cut, cover and skin, but is made of technical fabrics with reflective panels, glowing seam lines, magnetic clasps and chunky-soled boots.
POSTURE: standing.
COMPOSITION: a waist-up shot of her head, torso and hands; body in side profile, her face in profile too, not turned toward the camera, facing the right of the frame, so her own right side is toward the camera; camera low, near the ground — level with her face when she sits, kneels or lies on the floor or a bed, looking up at her when she stands; she is placed in the right third of the frame, open space of the place to her left.
Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand tucks hair behind her ear — her near arm, on the camera side; one unbroken arm from shoulder to hand, its forearm never hidden by a sleeve, bow or ornament.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand rests on her hip — her far arm, on the side away from the camera; one unbroken arm from shoulder to hand, its forearm never hidden by a sleeve, bow or ornament.
GAZE: her eyes are lowered.
EXPRESSION: one eye closed in a playful wink while the other stays open and bright, one mouth corner lifted in a small smile, brows relaxed.

Framing: a waist-up shot — the bottom edge crosses her waist; hips, legs and feet are out of frame.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia — and leave behind the object she holds in it; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

SIGNATURE ACCESSORY: her world's signature object — a set of bagpipes with clear crystal drones and chanter glowing soft violet — appears only as one small accessory shaped after it (a charm, brooch, pendant or hair ornament) or set down beside her in the scene; she does not hold it unless PROP names it.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, numbers, logo or watermark. Any animal or creature that belongs to the place stays separate from her at its own natural scale — never touching, held by or merged with her body.
